justifications.clinical.clinicalOutcomes: Protocolized weaning reduces ventilator days; PT/OT role in weaning team improves functional outcomes.
justifications.clinical.efficiency: ICU-specific training; institutional credentialing common; moderate time.
justifications.clinical.caseloadApplicability: Applicable specifically in ICU and acute care with ventilated patients; very narrow population.
justifications.clinical.reimbursement: Acute care respiratory therapy and early mobility billed through hospital DRG; no standalone PT code but supports ICU PT billing.
justifications.clinical.marketDemand: Valued in ICU and acute care PT/OT positions; expected competency in critical care specialty.
justifications.clinical.patientSatisfaction: Patients cannot self-report during ventilation; family reports reduced anxiety with active weaning plan.
justifications.business.cashPayViability: Hospital/ICU procedure; zero cash-pay consumer market.
justifications.business.pricingLeverage: Reimbursed inside facility per diems; no individual pricing leverage.
justifications.business.marketDifferentiation: Niche skill but only matters to acute-care employers, not consumers.
justifications.business.ownerLeverage: Cannot build a private practice around vent weaning; wrong setting entirely.
justifications.business.efficiency: Protocol training is relatively short, but irrelevant to entrepreneurship.
justifications.academicClinical.facultyRecognition: Valued for acute-care/cardiopulm faculty lines and ACS-track instructors but not a formal credential itself.
justifications.academicClinical.scholarship: Solid ICU rehab/early-mobility literature base for publications.
justifications.academicClinical.teachingValue: Directly strengthens acute care and cardiopulm course content in DPT curricula.
justifications.academicClinical.evidenceDepth: Strong RCT base on early mobilization and weaning protocols in ICU populations.
justifications.academicClinical.facultyDemand: Occasionally preferred for acute-care faculty roles but rarely explicitly required.
justifications.academicClinical.efficiency: Usually acquired through clinical experience rather than discrete cert; moderate efficiency.
